summary.name: Investment management (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing the professional management of securities and other assets for investors, covering industry structure, regulation, asset allocation and performance measurement.
use_cases: Understanding how professional investment managers operate
Learning about asset allocation and diversification
Reviewing SEC and FCA regulation of investment advisers
Studying fiduciary duties of fund managers
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software tool. It explains investment management as the professional handling of securities and other assets for institutional and private investors. It covers industry scope, the roles of fund managers, and the 3-P framework of philosophy, process and people. It describes asset allocation, investment styles, and performance metrics such as the Sharpe ratio, information ratio, alpha and multi-factor models. It also summarizes regulation in the United States, United Kingdom and parts of Asia.
notable: Explains the 3-P framework (philosophy, process, people) for judging managers
Covers risk-adjusted performance measures from Sharpe ratio to multi-factor models
Summarizes US, UK and Asian regulatory frameworks
caveats: Not a software tool; the listing describes it as money management software, which the page does not support
The article notes it needs more citations
Some sections are unevenly sourced and contain unclear wording
